missions.title: The Slipped Print
missions.knowledgeQuestion: How much of what we see in a copy comes from the way it was made?

objectives.title: Seat the ferry print on its pins and prepare a proof for its next reader.

dialogue.speaker: narrator
dialogue.text: A carrier is waiting for a ferry print. One sheet shows the river and jetties in dark ink. A thin sheet carries two red landing marks. Set the two together and someone can see the finished image. Two brass pins sit in the board.

options.text: Square the sheets at the lower corner and check the trial image.
Lay both sheets over the brass pins and check the image.

dialogue.speaker: narrator
dialogue.text: You square the bottom corners and smooth the sheets. The carrier moves back so you can see where the red marks fell.

dialogue.speaker: narrator
dialogue.text: The corners meet. A red landing mark now sits out in the river. 'It looks like a floating landing,' says a visitor. The printmaker runs a finger along the narrow upper sheet. It was trimmed after printing. The pinholes still show.

options.text: Lift the overlay and seat both holes on the pins.
Leave the trial on the board for now.

dialogue.speaker: narrator
dialogue.text: The trimmed corner sits inside the lower sheet. Both sheets stay still when you let go. The carrier waits for you to choose how the proof should travel.

dialogue.speaker: narrator
dialogue.text: The first pin holds the corner. The second stops the thin sheet turning. Both red marks now meet the ends of the drawn jetties. 'Our ferry crews use red for a place to board,' says the carrier. 'Cart crews read red as a place to stop. Give them the ferry key with either proof.'

options.text: Clip a joined proof and the ferry key to the carrier’s board for the shelter.
Slide the sheets into separate pockets for the next printer and put the key on top.
Leave the sheets on their pins for now.

dialogue.speaker: narrator
dialogue.text: The carrier lifts the joined image. At a glance, she can follow the two colours from the shore to the red marks. She points at the ferry key. A cart driver who had crossed out the red jetty puts it back on the walking route. The printmaker keeps the separate sheets at the bench so the next worker can still check how the mark moved.

dialogue.speaker: narrator
dialogue.text: The carrier marks the folder for the next printer. Each sheet can be lifted on its own. The next worker can see which block left which mark and fit both back onto the pins. The shelter will get a proof after the next printing, with the ferry key.

hints.text: The ferry image needs both sheets. Their cuts and their two holes give different places to start.
Find the print table on the west side of the hall. See where the red marks land when you bring the sheets together.
If the corners match and the marks drift, lift the thin sheet. Try its two holes on the two pins.
Once the marks reach the jetties, choose a joined copy for the shelter or two separate proofs for the worker.

journal.text: Two pinholes let the printed jetties and the red marks line up even after the paper had been trimmed. The joined proof was easier to see at a glance. The loose sheets let a printer check how the picture was made.

moments.did: You changed the way you lined up the print after seeing where its red marks landed.
